rules.title: Positive finite structural PK parameters
rules.scientific_rationale: Clearances, physiological distribution volumes, inter-compartmental flows, rate constants, and half-lives represent physical mass-transfer rates or spaces and must be finite and strictly positive (> 0).
rules.recommendation: Constrain structural PK parameters to strictly positive finite domains (e.g., log-scale parameterization or positive lower bounds).
rules.reference_basis: Fundamental mass-balance and compartmental pharmacokinetic definition (Rowland & Tozer, Clinical Pharmacokinetics and Pharmacodynamics).

rules.title: Unit compatibility and deterministic normalization
rules.scientific_rationale: Every dimensional PK parameter must carry an explicit, unambiguous unit compatible with its physical dimension (flow for CL/Q, volume or weight-normalized volume for V, inverse time for rate constants, time for half-life, dimensionless fraction or percent for F).
rules.recommendation: Supply explicit, dimensionally compatible units for every model parameter before comparing against physiological thresholds.
rules.reference_basis: Dimensional analysis and pharmacometric reporting standards (FDA Population Pharmacokinetics Guidance).

rules.title: Absolute bioavailability F within (0, 1]
rules.scientific_rationale: Absolute systemic bioavailability F represents the fraction of administered dose reaching systemic circulation and is bounded by (0, 1] (or (0, 100]% when typed as percent). Values > 1.0 are only plausible when F represents relative bioavailability against a lower-exposure reference formulation.
rules.recommendation: Use logit transformation to constrain absolute F to (0, 1), or document relative bioavailability if F > 1.0 is intentional.
rules.reference_basis: Rowland & Tozer, Clinical Pharmacokinetics and Pharmacodynamics (Bioavailability definition).

rules.title: Systemic clearance CL compared with context-scaled hepatic blood flow and cardiac output
rules.scientific_rationale: For a systemically cleared drug (distinguished from apparent oral CL/F), systemic clearance exceeding context-scaled hepatic blood flow (~90 L/h in a 70 kg adult) implies substantial extrahepatic elimination (e.g., renal + hepatic, pulmonary, or blood esterase hydrolysis) or high blood-to-plasma partitioning. Exceeding cardiac output (~300 L/h) is physiologically extreme.
rules.recommendation: Verify whether the parameter is apparent oral clearance (CL/F) rather than systemic CL, check unit scaling, or document extrahepatic/blood-esterase clearance.
rules.reference_basis: Davies & Morris 1993 (Physiological parameters in laboratory animals and humans, Pharm Res 10:1093-1095); Wilkinson & Shand 1975.

rules.title: Renal clearance CL_R compared with glomerular filtration and effective renal plasma flow
rules.scientific_rationale: Passive renal filtration clearance cannot exceed fu * GFR (~7.5 L/h * fu in a healthy 70 kg adult). Renal clearance exceeding fu * GFR implies active tubular secretion; renal clearance exceeding effective renal plasma flow (~36 L/h = 600 mL/min in a 70 kg adult) is physiologically implausible unless blood-to-plasma partitioning is high.
rules.recommendation: Document active tubular secretion if CL_R > fu * GFR, or re-examine CL_R parameterization and units if CL_R exceeds effective renal plasma flow.
rules.reference_basis: Davies & Morris 1993; Rowland & Tozer (Renal elimination mechanisms).

rules.title: Central volume Vc compared with plasma volume floor and tissue ceiling
rules.scientific_rationale: Central volume of distribution Vc cannot be smaller than vascular plasma volume (~0.043 L/kg, screening floor 0.03 L/kg or ~2.1 L in a 70 kg adult). Extremely large systemic Vc (> 20-50 L/kg) implies extensive peripheral tissue/lipid sequestration or confusion with apparent volume Vc/F.
rules.recommendation: Check whether Vc is less than plasma volume due to unit error (e.g., L/kg labeled as L), or whether high Vc reflects apparent oral Vc/F with low bioavailability.
rules.reference_basis: Davies & Morris 1993; Oie & Tozer 1979 (Volume of distribution relationships).

rules.title: Steady-state volume Vss consistency with physiological spaces and compartmental sum
rules.scientific_rationale: Steady-state volume Vss must be at least plasma volume (~0.03 L/kg floor) and, when compartmental volumes (Vc, Vp, Vp2) are simultaneously reported, must equal Vc + sum(Vp) within numerical tolerance.
rules.recommendation: Ensure Vss = Vc + sum(Vp) in mammillary models and verify absolute (L) versus weight-normalized (L/kg) volume units.
rules.reference_basis: Gibaldi & Perrier, Pharmacokinetics (Steady-state volume of distribution in mammillary models).

rules.title: Terminal/effective half-life consistency with clearance and volume
rules.scientific_rationale: In linear compartmental models, half-life is deterministically linked to clearance and volume (t1/2 = ln(2)*Vc/CL for 1-compartment, or ln(2)/beta for multi-compartment). Reported half-life diverging from model parameters indicates calculation or unit error.
rules.recommendation: Recompute terminal half-life from the macro-rate eigenvalues (alpha, beta) or ln(2)*V/CL using consistent time and volume units.
rules.reference_basis: Gabrielsson & Weiner, Pharmacokinetic and Pharmacodynamic Data Analysis.

rules.title: Absorption rate constant ka bounds and flip-flop kinetics check
rules.scientific_rationale: First-order absorption rate constant ka outside typical physiological absorption rates ([0.05, 10] h^-1) or ka <= elimination rate ke (CL/Vc) indicates potential flip-flop kinetics or unidentifiable rapid absorption.
rules.recommendation: If ka <= ke, verify whether flip-flop kinetics are expected (e.g., extended-release or subcutaneous depot) or constrain ka > ke for immediate-release formulations.
rules.reference_basis: Yanez et al. 2011 (Flip-flop pharmacokinetics:delivering a reversal of disposition, Ther Deliv 2:643-672).

rules.title: Allometric body-weight exponent on clearance (CL, Q) near 0.75
rules.scientific_rationale: Theory-based allometric scaling relates metabolic/elimination flows (CL, Q) to body weight with an exponent near 0.75 (typical empirical range 0.60-0.90). Large deviations often reflect collinearity with age/maturation or sparse weight range.
rules.recommendation: Consider fixing the allometric clearance exponent to 0.75 or document empirical justification and covariate precision.
rules.reference_basis: Anderson & Holford 2008 (Mechanism-based concepts of size and maturity in pharmacokinetics, Annu Rev Pharmacol Toxicol 48:303-332).

rules.title: Allometric body-weight exponent on volume (Vc, Vp, Vss) near 1.0
rules.scientific_rationale: Theory-based allometric scaling relates distribution volumes (Vc, Vp, Vss) proportionally to body mass with an exponent near 1.0 (typical range 0.80-1.20). Deviations outside this range require strong empirical support.
rules.recommendation: Consider fixing the allometric volume exponent to 1.0 or document body-composition rationale.
rules.reference_basis: Anderson & Holford 2008 (Annu Rev Pharmacol Toxicol 48:303-332).

rules.title: Inter-individual variability (IIV omega^2 / %CV) magnitude plausibility
rules.scientific_rationale: Log-normal IIV exceeding 100% CV (omega^2 > 0.693) or 200% CV (omega^2 > 1.609) often indicates structural misspecification, unmodeled subpopulations/outliers, or poor identifiability (e.g., on ka or Vp).
rules.recommendation: Inspect eta distributions, shrinkage, and outlier subjects; verify whether high IIV is driven by unmodeled covariates or bioavailability variability.
rules.reference_basis: Mould & Upton 2013 (Basic concepts in population modeling, simulation, and model-based drug development, CPT Pharmacometrics Syst Pharmacol).

rules.title: Random-effect variance terms (omega^2, sigma^2) finite and nonnegative
rules.scientific_rationale: Variance of any real-valued random variable must be finite and nonnegative (>= 0). Negative variance is a mathematical impossibility.
rules.recommendation: Correct negative or non-finite variance estimates before accepting or simulating from the model.
rules.reference_basis: Probability theory axiom (Var(X) >= 0).

rules.title: Omega and Sigma covariance matrices symmetric and positive semidefinite (PSD)
rules.scientific_rationale: Any valid covariance or correlation matrix must be square, symmetric, and positive semidefinite (all eigenvalues >= 0). Non-PSD matrices cannot represent a real multivariate random-effect distribution and fail Cholesky factorization.
rules.recommendation: Re-estimate Omega/Sigma with a Cholesky or log-Cholesky parameterization, or reduce block structure if covariance is boundary-collapsed.
rules.reference_basis: Matrix analysis and mixed-effects statistical theory (Pinheiro & Bates, Mixed-Effects Models in S and S-PLUS).

rules.title: Random-effect correlations r_ij within [-1, 1] and collinearity screen
rules.scientific_rationale: By Cauchy-Schwarz inequality, correlation coefficients r_ij must lie in [-1, 1]. Correlations with |r_ij| >= 0.95 indicate near-singular Omega blocks and over-parameterization.
rules.recommendation: Ensure |r_ij| <= 1.0; if |r_ij| >= 0.95, consider shared-eta parameterization or diagonal Omega.
rules.reference_basis: Cauchy-Schwarz inequality; Mould & Upton 2013.

rules.title: Residual unexplained variability (RUV) nonnegativity and magnitude screen
rules.scientific_rationale: Residual error terms must be finite and nonnegative, cannot be identically zero across all active error components, and proportional RUV exceeding 50-100% CV suggests severe model misspecification or data errors.
rules.recommendation: Inspect CWRES/IWRES diagnostics, bioanalytical assay LLOQ, and dosing/sampling time records if residual error is extreme.
rules.reference_basis: Karlsson & Savic 2007 (Diagnosing model diagnostics, Clin Pharmacol Ther 82:17-20).

rules.title: Monoclonal antibody (mAb) central volume Vc near vascular plasma space
rules.scientific_rationale: IgG monoclonal antibodies (~150 kDa) are largely restricted to vascular plasma and interstitial fluid; central volume Vc typically approximates plasma volume (~0.04-0.08 L/kg, or ~2.8-5.6 L in a 70 kg adult).
rules.recommendation: Verify mAb Vc units and bioavailability adjustment (Vc vs Vc/F for SC dosing) if Vc deviates substantially from 0.03-0.10 L/kg.
rules.reference_basis: Dirks & Meibohm 2010 (Population pharmacokinetics of therapeutic monoclonal antibodies, Clin Pharmacokinet 49:633-659).

rules.title: Monoclonal antibody (mAb) linear clearance CL within FcRn-protected catabolic range
rules.scientific_rationale: Due to FcRn salvage, linear proteolytic clearance of IgG mAbs in reference adults is slow (~0.15-0.60 L/day = 0.006-0.025 L/h, screening window 0.003-0.05 L/h). Small-molecule-like clearance (> 0.15 L/h) is implausible for linear mAb elimination unless confusion between L/day and L/h or dominant TMDD occurred.
rules.recommendation: Check whether mAb CL was reported in L/day but labeled as L/h, or document nonlinear target-mediated drug disposition (TMDD).
rules.reference_basis: Dirks & Meibohm 2010 (Clin Pharmacokinet 49:633-659); Deng et al. 2011.

rules.title: Inter-compartmental flow Q and micro-rate constant (k10, k12, k21) mass-balance consistency
rules.scientific_rationale: In mammillary compartmental models, micro-rate constants are exact ratios of clearance/flow to compartment volumes (k10 = CL/Vc, k12 = Q/Vc, k21 = Q/Vp), and inter-compartmental distribution flow Q cannot physically exceed cardiac output.
rules.recommendation: Ensure micro-rate constants match Q/Vc, Q/Vp, and CL/Vc using identical volume and time units.
rules.reference_basis: Gibaldi & Perrier, Pharmacokinetics (Linear mammillary compartmental systems).

rules.title: Model predictions (PRED/IPRED) finite, nonnegative, and within physical concentration ceiling
rules.scientific_rationale: Predicted drug concentrations (PRED, IPRED) represent physical mass per unit volume and must be finite (no NaN or Inf) and nonnegative (>= 0).
rules.recommendation: Check ODE solver tolerances, parameter domain bounds, and dosing inputs if negative or non-finite concentrations occur.
rules.reference_basis: Physical conservation of mass and positivity of compartmental ODE systems.
